title: Ctrl+S saves nothing outside the script editor — CSV grid has dirty tracking but no save shortcut
existing_state: ProcessCmdKey (Form1.cs:14450-14480) handles Ctrl+S only when txtCommand or txtPreset has focus, calling SaveCurrentPreset (14454-14460); with focus anywhere else — including the host grid — Ctrl+S is silently swallowed and does nothing. Yet the CSV grid maintains full dirty tracking (_csvDirty), has Save/SaveAs plumbing (SaveCurrentCsv/SaveCsvAs, 9245-9325), and guards exit with a save prompt (TryResolvePendingCsvChangesForExit, 14919-14945). A user who just pasted 200 rows and habitually hits Ctrl+S gets no save and no feedback, and only learns about the unsaved state at exit time.
recommendation: In the Ctrl+S case, add a grid-focused branch: when dgv_variables (or its editing control) contains focus and a CSV file is loaded, call SaveCurrentCsv(); when no path exists yet, fall through to SaveCsvAs. Optionally flash the saved filename in the status bar as confirmation. Consider Ctrl+Shift+S for Save As to round out the convention.
user_benefit: The universal save shortcut works where users expect it; bulk grid edits stop living dangerously until app exit.

evidence.note: Ctrl+S gated on txtCommand/txtPreset focus only
SaveCurrentCsv/SaveCsvAs plumbing exists and is shortcut-less
exit-time CSV save prompt proves dirty tracking exists
